A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite additions and rearrangements.

before.justification: v1 reports original character-generation and layout experiments, ablations, generated handwriting examples, and a 20-participant subjective study.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds cross-line reference experiments, end-to-end generation examples and failures, and a revised subjective study.

M1.justification: v1 only proposes end-to-end generation as future work; v3 Appendix A.3 implements an exploratory variant by concatenating character embeddings into a full-line embedding for the U-Net generator. This changes conditioning and generation procedure, while the primary layout generator, glyph synthesizer, and training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The CASIA-OLHWDB and ICDAR-2013 datasets remain unchanged. v3 adds evaluation using a reference from another line by the same writer and explicitly tests inter-character connected handwriting in Appendix A.3. Its mathematical-expression applicability claim is not accompanied by an experiment.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 10 adds an explicit qualitative character comparison against SDT, which previously appeared only in the quantitative comparison. Table 1 retains DeepImitator, DiffWriter, FontRNN, WriteLikeU, and SDT; the Gaussian and Unconditional layout comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported subjective study changes from ten real/generated pairs to fifteen described pairs, while Figure 8 now shows one real and two synthetic rows per block; both versions use 20 participants. Appendix A.4 adds a controlled comparison of ten target-line boxes versus ten boxes from another same-writer line. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 add substantive investigations of two central issues: whether end-to-end generation can produce connected strokes and where it fails, and whether layout imitation depends on using the target line as context. Figures 12–14 and Table 5 substantially extend the analysis beyond the retained contrastive-learning, reference-length, and layout case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain single-value reporting; the subjective-study sample-count change is an evaluation-design change.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged. Table 3 swaps AR and CR entries, including In-Context from 0.857/0.852 to 0.852/0.857. v3 adds nearly matching cross-line-prefix results in Table 5 and qualitative SDT and end-to-end findings. The subjective response rate changes from over 90% to over 85% under a revised protocol, so this does not establish a comparable performance decline.

T1.justification: The conditional-independence assumption, probability factorization, autoregressive equations, training objectives, DDPM derivation, and AR/CR definitions remain unchanged. The Table 3 correction changes reported values, not the metric definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: hierarchical text-line generation, in-context layout imitation, and diffusion-based glyph synthesis with multi-scale style encoding. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a concrete tradeoff between connected-stroke generation and instability on longer sequences. Appendix A.4 explains cross-line reference success through consistent same-writer layout style and adds an untested claim about simple 2D expressions. The primary method's limitation on inter-character cursive connections remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds a promised public-code repository location and explicitly identifies the first ten ground-truth boxes as Figure 7's context prefix. Existing architecture dimensions, preprocessing, hardware, learning rates, and training duration remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the promised code was released.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2023), AffGANwriting, in connection with feature fusion. Appendix A.4 expands the comparison between learned contextual layout generation and manually designed model-free approaches. The broader related-work coverage and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introduction edits, a rewritten subjective-study paragraph, new appendix subsections, and publication, author-contact, and acknowledgment updates. Qualitative results become Section 4.3.3 rather than Section 4.4, but the main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Experimental visual presentation is substantially expanded and reorganized: the subjective-study figure is replaced with author blocks, Figure 7 is redrawn and clarified, and SDT, end-to-end, failure-case, and cross-line-prefix displays plus Table 5 are added. The earlier three-writer visualization moves from v1 Figure 8 to v3 Figure 11; it is not removed.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.4 strengthens validation by testing references from another same-writer line, while Appendix A.3 makes the connected-stroke versus stability tradeoff concrete. Table 3 also aligns AR/CR ordering with the unchanged definitions. These provide useful gains in evidence and transparency, although the revised subjective-study description remains ambiguous about pairs versus three-row blocks, and the new 2D-expression claim is untested.
